Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Warden armor
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: The Power Armor of a Custodian Warden, an elite warrior even among the Ten Thousand, its red robe symbolizing their status. \n\nA Custodian must have at least five centuries of continuous service to become a Warden. Every oath sworn by a new Warden is personally written after a year of meditation, upon which they receive their characteristic red robe.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Castellan plate
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description:
A replica of the Castellan Plate, an ancient and legendary suit of Custodian Power Armor. The auramite armor plating can shrug off almost any threat, and the lion-hide cloak is strengthened with adamantium thread - it flows like cloth, but cannot be pierced or cut by any normal weapon. 

The true Castellan Plate is worn by Trajann Valoris, the Captain-General of the Adeptus Custodes. Unusually for a Custodian, he believed in offensive defense - sallying forth to destroy threats to the Imperium before they could threaten the Throneworld. 

He rose to power during the Years of Madness, a crisis on Terra that saw two successive Captain-Generals dead or gone, a massive spike in dangerous cultist activity, and a widespread maddening of servitors in the Dark Cells that forced wholesale euthanization.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Blade Champion armor
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: Special Power Armor crafted for Blade Champions of the Adeptus Custodes. \n\nThe task of a Blade Champion is to seek and slay the enemy's commanders and heroes. For this task, they are bestowed with the mighty Vaultsword, and the expertise needed to wield them to great effect. Many names are inscribed upon the Tome Eternal, every one of them belonging to a Blade Champion.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Eye of the Emperor armor
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A light suit of Power Armor worn on rare occasion by an Eye of the Emperor. \n\nEyes of the Emperor are Custodians that have "retired", due to advanced age or grievous, permanent wounds. Their role is to watch the galaxy for threats that may endanger the Emperor, and to report any such threats to the Captain-General of the Adeptus Custodes.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Warden helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: The helmet of a Custodian Warden. It is roughly similar to that of the Hykanatoi, and is wrought of just as much quality, if not more. \n\nNever shall the Adeptus Custodes cease their protection of the Emperor. The thought of failure simply does not cross their mind.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Castellan helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: An auramite Power Armor helmet supposed to be worn with the Castellan Plate. While it is typically not worn, as the Captain-General usually shows his face to inspire other Custodians, it can still provide excellent protection against all threats. \n\nAfter serving in the Allarus Terminators, a young Trajann Valoris was made a Companion - the three hundred elite Custodians assigned as the Emperor's personal guard. However, due to his desire to take the initiative against the Great Enemy, he lasted only twenty-two years before becoming a Shield-Captain - and, a few centuries later, rising to the rank of Captain-General.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Sagittarum helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: An uncommon helmet worn by Sagittarum Custodians of the Adeptus Custodes. The Sagittarum Guard are a rarer type of Custodian, focusing on delivering heavy firepower from longer ranges, like the various fire support squads of the Adeptus Astartes. \n\nDuring the Great Crusade and Horus Heresy, they stood guard on the outermost perimeter of the Imperial Palace, on guard for any invader. However, they became a rare Sight in the 41st Millennium.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Venatari mask
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A lightweight but still very protective battle mask, worn by the Venatari jump-infantry of the Adeptus Custodes.\n\nEach Venatari is a highly-skilled veteran of the Blood Games, a special wargame practiced by the Adeptus Custodes. Certain Custodians are tasked with mock-assassinating the Emperor, allowing them to find and exploit security weaknesses which can then be patched. Some Blood Games have been known to last years - one Custodian, Calladayce Taurovalia Kesh, ended her Blood Game after over two years when she was caught trying to teleport a cyclonic warhead into the Emperor's throne room.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Blade Champion helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: An auramite-plated helmet worn by a Custodian Blade Champion. Against the most threatening foes the enemy can muster, great protection is required. \n\nThe Blade Champion is second-in-command of a Shield Company, second to the Shield-Captain. While their Captain maintains control of the main force, Blade Champions can be found leading smaller detachments into battle, plunging deep into the enemy's ranks.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Eye of the Emperor helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description: A light Power Armor helmet, combined with a hood - suitable for an Eye of the Emperor. \n\nThough they are no longer suited to the regular ranks of the Adeptus Custodes, an Eye of the Emperor retains their biological and genetic enhancements. Many Eyes could still slay a Chaos Space Marine man-to-man, and are more than a match for the majority of the everyday threats an Imperial underhive citizen sees.

Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.label: Shield Captain helmet
Core40k.AlternateBaseFormDef.description:
The helmet of a Shield-Captain of the Adeptus Custodes, with extra markings to symbolise their rank. 

Shield-Captains are the leaders of Shield Companies, the standard tactical formation of the Adeptus Custodes - multiple Shield Companies form a Shield Host. However, their organisation is conducted with surprising looseness, with Shield Companies being formed and disbanded as needed, and Shield-Captains have even been known to command each other as the situation requires. 

Custodians do not require orders to fall in line, nor rank to command - every Custodian knows their place and respects each others' authority.
